sentences.text: Fukuiraptor was a relatively lightly built animal, indicated by its slender phalanges.
The holotype possessed very large, flat hand claws that were initially mistaken for foot claws, leading to its early classification as a dromaeosaurid.
Its teeth resemble carcharodontosaurids in being compressed, blade-like, and having wrinkled enamel, and tyrannosaurids in having oblique blood grooves near serrations.
Researchers believe the type specimen was immature and that adults of Fukuiraptor may have been larger.
The type specimen, a partial skeleton designated FPDM-V97122, was discovered in the Kitadani quarry near Katsuyama in Fukui Prefecture.
Numerous humeri, femurs, and teeth from other individuals have been found in the same quarry and assigned to Fukuiraptor.
A tooth designated NDC-P0001 found in the Sebayashi Formation has been referred to Fukuiraptor.
Most other individuals found at the locality were juveniles, with the smallest being less than a quarter the size of the holotype.
Fukuiraptor was initially classified as a dromaeosaurid and considered a carnosaur related to Allosaurus.
Recent studies classify Fukuiraptor as a megaraptoran, potentially part of the family Neovenatoridae.
Fukuiraptor lived from the Hauterivian to the Aptian, between 132.6 and 113.2 million years ago.
Fukuiraptor is considered either one of the earliest members of Megaraptora or a close relative of Australovenator.
